method.interface: Installed Windows game, using visible UI only for all gameplay choices, movement, rewards, forging, shops, save/profile navigation, and meta purchases.
method.profiles: Three separate empty slots in an isolated APPDATA directory. No actual player saves touched.
method.knowledge: First attempt approached through on-screen instructions; later attempts use lessons learned through play. No gameplay source read by root before all three attempts finished.
method.scope: Brass Frontier Easy / Act I, the only difficulty available on an empty profile. Each clear is a game-defined victory. These are not claims of three full three-act clears.
method.supplemental: Independent code-driven class audits and hidden render/regression tests are separate evidence, not counted as UI playtests.

observations.finding: Region and difficulty locks are large and legible. Hero passive text and class-deck inspection explain initial choice. Timeline footer explains firing at the tile's right edge.
observations.assessment: Opening UI was navigable without reading code or an external guide.

observations.finding: Single-click rewards equipped when space existed and went to storage when full. A third Spark Shot opened its upgrade choice and consumed the reward plus two owned copies.
observations.assessment: Core flow worked; successful reward combine still required a redundant empty-arena Continue in baseline.

observations.finding: Different-width timeline dragging moved neighboring tiles. A stored Cover swapped with same-width Line Guard. Storage and sequence blocks kept contiguous widths.
observations.assessment: Movement was practical; storage/forge hover copy used an older tooltip style.

observations.finding: Starshot fired from a distance, retreated while facing her target, and emitted visible shots from the weapon. Critical numbers were gold and larger. Enemies visibly prepared named attacks and repairs. Victory animation appeared before rewards.
observations.assessment: The three heroes were visually recognizable and played differently; no visible animation blocker found.

observations.finding: Long reward descriptions scrolled despite spare vertical space; Armor Crush's final conditional clause was initially hidden. Forge tooltips added large Beat/Reach/Range glossary blocks over the tree.
observations.assessment: Important ability text needed more space and consistent hover treatment.

observations.finding: Elite relic artwork was tiny and claims were far below their descriptions, leaving a large empty middle area. A tile-after footer did not match the subsequent draft.
observations.assessment: The tile-after label belonged to a different relic card, not to the selected relic; its separated position made it read as a global preview. Removed the preview labels while preserving companion reward mechanics.

observations.finding: Save/title/resume retained the manually rearranged loadout. Each independent slot earned its own Marks and Medium unlock. Slot 3 bought Stout Start, Gravity Hook, and Tile Enchantments between runs for 21 Marks total.
observations.assessment: No save loss, crash, or progression blocker observed in the three attempts.

observations.finding: The third final-boss draft offered two Cover variants plus a Line Guard variant with the same Chorus Clinic name.
observations.assessment: Distinct base upgrade trees should be preferred within one boss draft.

fixes.change: Reuse full illustrated ability cards for storage and forge, remove duplicated beat/range glossary.
Group larger borderless relic art, name, description, and claim close together; preserve compact/multihero layout.
Show actual tile ability text instead of appending relic positioning advice to it.
Use available overlay height for descriptions, retain access to full copy.
Valid next-path click applies fitting reward upgrade and advances after transactional save; retain manual arrangement and save-failure safeguards.
Keep three-hero sequences and existing targeting controls reachable in compact windows, including narrow/wide tiles and storage.
Prefer distinct base tile upgrade trees for boss Legendary offers; keep deterministic rarity/class/unlock rules and safe undersized-pool fallback.
Update class audit to the current transactional single-copy camp upgrade API.
Move the existing Practice title/result exit from the footer to the top-left header; preserve campaign Save & title and Retry in Practice return behavior.

balance.human_results_note: 3/3 Easy wins in this small sample are not a population win-rate estimate. Warden was much safer than the two other builds; Starshot nearly died, Hexwright needed recovery decisions.

independent_audit.limitations: Heuristic pilot choices do not predict human win rates. Results describe the baseline before boss draft diversity changes.

remaining_priorities: Warden's Bash-family passive rarely participates in bespoke shield builds: 15 of 16 audited Medium final builds had no Bash family. Validate a shield-aligned eligibility change separately.
Rune Smith warrants targeted human playtest: audited Medium first-boss10/16, Hard full-run0/16, versus Cantor16/16 and12/16. Do not tune solely from bots.

Class root decks still share substantial content: Warden/Bulwark share14/20 Common roots, Lancer/Duelist13/20. Bespoke class mechanics are a stronger next content investment than more generic variants.

game_suites.notes: One integrated full run after reward, layout, and boss draft fixes. Later small Practice exit change passed the two directly affected Arena Lab and checkpoint suites again.

boss_draft_checks.coverage: Initial and paid-reroll root diversity, deterministic class/act/party/unlock contexts, signatures, small pools, and save compatibility.

retest.render_checks: Hidden GPU verification of full relic descriptions, long Armor Crush copy, compact three-hero sequences, width-one through width-five inventory geometry and targeting, and full storage popup.
retest.packed_build: 104 actors, 93 native motions, 18 additional hero actions, 24 hero reactions, 745 tile effects, 144 particle frames verified.

live_candidate_ui.runtime: Candidate exported pack run in Godot 4.7.2; release executable intentionally blocks main-pack override.
